title: Momentum and Impulse
seo_title: Physics 12: Momentum and Impulse Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Momentum is conserved within a closed and isolated system: momentum, impulse and change in momentum, conservation of momentum in collisions and explosions, and elastic and inelastic collisions. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Physics 12)
meta_desc: Free Physics 12 worksheets (BC Curriculum): momentum, impulse and collisions. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Total momentum is conserved in a closed system.
body_html:
How to think about it

Momentum p = mv is a vector. Impulse is FΔt and equals the change in momentum. A longer stopping time means a smaller force, which is why airbags and helmets protect us.

In a closed, isolated system the total momentum before a collision equals the total after. In an elastic collision kinetic energy is also conserved; in an inelastic collision some is changed to heat and sound; in a perfectly inelastic collision the objects stick together.

Example

A 1000 kg car moves at 20 m/s. What is its momentum?

p = mv

Answer: 20 000 kg·m/s

Example

A 2 kg cart at 3 m/s hits and sticks to a stationary 1 kg cart. Final speed?

6 = 3v

Answer: 2 m/s

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting that momentum has direction.
  • Thinking kinetic energy is always conserved.
  • Mixing up impulse and force.

faq.q: Why do you bend your knees when you land?
faq.a: It increases the stopping time and lowers the force.

faq.q: How does a rocket move in space?
faq.a: It pushes exhaust backward, so the rocket gains equal forward momentum.

items.q: A 0.5 kg ball moving at 5 m/s is stopped by an average force of 125 N. How long does the stop take?

A 5 kg bowling ball moving at 6 m/s is brought to a stop. What impulse acts on it?
A 6 kg gun fires a 0.0500 kg bullet at 550 m/s. What is the recoil speed of the gun?
items.e: Momentum is conserved: MV = mv, V = 0.0500 × 550 ÷ 6 = 4.58 m/s.
